content.question: What is the main difference between an RNN and a feedforward neural network?
options: RNNs have loop-back connections that maintain internal memory, while FNNs process data in one direction.
RNNs process all inputs in parallel, while FNNs process them sequentially.
RNNs use convolutional filters, while FNNs use attention.
RNNs cannot be applied to sequential data, while FNNs can.
content.answer: RNNs have loop-back connections that maintain internal memory, while FNNs process data in one direction.
